headline: Monday session: measured moves and the evidence still needed

entries.happened: No verified company-specific event was established for the 9 November session from the dated sources checked; the measured bar is the evidence.
entries.why: The daily bar measures the market outcome but does not identify its cause. The investment case still depends on revenue growth, margins, balance-sheet capacity and valuation. A one-session move can reflect sector positioning, macro rates or liquidity rather than a change in company fundamentals. This distinction is especially important because the November 3 index move was narrow and election-sensitive. Investors should therefore test the thesis against company-level evidence, not infer a durable change from the aggregate tape. The absence of a verified event is itself the honest result of the research window.
entries.priced_in: The price already incorporates the observed November 3 close and its session return. Any broad AI, rates or election narrative remains an inference until company disclosures and subsequent trading confirm that investors changed expected cash flows.
entries.would_change: A dated filing, earnings release, guidance change, material contract, regulatory action or an unusual multi-session move with confirming volume would change this reading.
entries.next_date: Unscheduled watch: next company filing or earnings release; monitor the next completed NYSE session.

macro.dd: AP reported that the S&P 500 rose 0.4% while most constituents fell, with Nvidia and Broadcom among the strongest supports. Reuters reported the Dow fell 0.38% and Nasdaq gained 0.83%. This edition records the twelve company bars separately and does not assign company causation without verified events.

readthrough.heading: Measured tape, conditional narrative
readthrough.title: What the completed session can and cannot show
readthrough.body: Across these twelve companies, the daily bars establish price, range and volume for November 3. Research checks found no verified company-specific event for this edition. The market backdrop was a narrow technology-led rebound ahead of the US midterm result, so breadth and later filings are the tests for whether fundamentals changed.
